title: AI Accounting Automation in Excel: Preparing Tax Resolution Workpapers
summary: A practical guide to organizing and reviewing spreadsheet-based financial workpapers for tax resolution cases.
body_markdown:
Tax resolution professionals often use spreadsheets to organize deposits, expenses, and supporting records before preparing a collection form. The spreadsheet is a workpaper, not the source of truth: each number needs a defined period and a supporting document. This distinction matters when using automation to prepare financial workpapers.


## Set up a reviewable workbook


Keep source references, transaction dates, descriptions, proposed categories, and reviewer notes in distinct columns. Separate raw records from calculations and final figures. If you adjust an expense or exclude a transfer, document the reason rather than silently replacing the original entry.


## Use automation at the handoff


Rima’s current tax resolution workflow focuses on reading client financial documents and preparing 433-F, 433-B, and 433-A (OIC) drafts for human review. It also supports[self-employed P&L assembly](https://www.getrima.ai/resources/case-study/p-and-l-assembly) . Those workflows can inform spreadsheet-based review, but should not be confused with a claim that Rima edits arbitrary Excel templates or integrates with every accounting system.


Before moving figures from a workpaper into a form, reconcile the period, check unexplained transactions, and compare totals with the underlying statements. An enrolled agent or case manager should resolve any discrepancy and approve the resulting entries.


## Choose a useful first metric


Measure preparation and review time separately. A workpaper that is assembled faster but requires extensive correction may not improve the overall process. Track the number of open questions at review and whether a reviewer can locate each supporting record. See[the ROI guide](https://www.getrima.ai/blog/tax-resolution-firm-roi) for a simple calculation framework.
